channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
item.description: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
item.description: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘The money didn’t work’: Big Tech’s $600mn midterm campaign falls flat
item.description: Elon Musk rebuked as anger at AI and Silicon Valley fuels support for Democrats

item.title: [EU Observer] Two fatal train disasters in less than a year: I never thought I would see this happen in my native Spain
item.description: As Spain’s transport minister resigns and politicians trade accusations over budgets and responsibility, many ordinary Spaniards are left wondering why the safety systems failed - and how the country could suffer 115 railway deaths in a single year.

item.title: [EU Observer] Afghan pushback survivor fights ‘impossible’ evidence rules in European courts with new UN case against Greece
item.description: The EU's human rights court rejected a case from an Afghan pushback survivor who was just 15 years old when he was turned back to Turkey by the Hellenic coast guard. The impossibility of achieving justice on the systematic practice against migrants of all ages was highlighted by the European court's inadmission, as the young survivor was forced to appeal to the UN's human rights courts instead.

item.title: [EU Observer] Moldova seen as ‘best performer’ on EU-accession reforms, despite onslaught of Russian sabotage
item.description: Chișinău's progress took place against a backdrop of growing hybrid attacks from Russia, such as drones entering the country’s airspace, cyberattacks, and Moldovan citizens recruited to perform sabotage.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia fails in bid to reverse ban on its ships using Europe’s docks and locks
item.description: Russian authorities challenged restrictive measures imposed by EU ministers against ships approved by the St Petersburg ship-certifying body. The EU's General Court rejected a bid to overturn the ban, but left the door open for future recognition of the authority.

item.title: [EU Observer] Energy tax and carbon emissions law on chopping block as EU Commission doubles down on ‘simplification’ drive
item.description: More than 30 laws will be mothballed or repealed, the EU Commission announced on Wednesday, as its deregulation agenda continues to gather pace.

item.title: [EU Observer] Lame duck or angry duck? Europe’s leadership largely silent on Trump’s election disaster, fearing backlash
item.description: Sweeping US mid-term election wins by the Democrats have earned only muted or scattered responses and reactions from Europe's leadership.

item.title: [DW] Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
item.description: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: [DW] Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
item.description: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

item.title: [DW] Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

item.title: [DW] Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins post-election clean-up
item.description: The landslide victory of the Students' List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

item.title: [DW] Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
item.description: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

item.title: [DW] European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

item.title: [Financial Times] Los Angeles elects democratic socialist Nithya Raman as mayor
item.description: Win follows Zohran Mamdani’s rise in New York and resounding victories by other progressives in Washington and Providence

item.title: [Financial Times] Wall Street sheds $3.2tn as Democratic midterm sweep triggers brutal AI rout
item.description: Tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 tumbles 6.4% in day of chaotic trading

item.title: [Financial Times] Will Democrats stall the AI boom?
item.description: Newly elected officials have pledged to curb data centre construction, rattling the trade that has powered US stock markets

item.title: [Financial Times] Wall Street mega-donors clobbered by Democratic sweep
item.description: Top hedge fund managers and private equity executives spent more than $300mn on Republican campaigns to little or no effect

item.title: [Financial Times] Tech leaders need an urgent rethink of their political strategy
item.description: America’s data centre backlash is emblematic of AI anxiety and a scepticism of the industry’s power and wealth

item.title: [EU Observer] Internal energy papers show “half-hearted” EU commission efforts to save methane rules
item.description: As ambassadors meet again to decide how long to delay the EU’s methane rules, internal documents show how the commission did too little to save them.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU targets large firms to unlock budget deal
item.description: European Council President António Costa hopes the concessions will facilitate an agreement on the bloc's next long-term budget.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage criticizes Trump’s ‘broken promise’ on foreign wars after midterms kicking
item.description: The Reform UK leader is increasingly distancing himself from the U.S. president as cost-of-living pressures hit Britons.

item.title: [Euractiv] Denmark, Portugal and Spain call for ambitious digital fairness rules
item.description: The Digital Fairness Act is set to be proposed by the European Commission on 11 November

item.title: [Financial Times] European stocks overtake Wall Street following Democratic sweep
item.description: Stoxx Europe 600 index ahead of S&P 500 for this year as US stocks tumble

item.title: [Euractiv] NATO hosts second Brussels talks on Ukraine security guarantees
item.description: The talks focused on possible security guarantees, Ukraine's representative said

item.title: [Financial Times] Nasdaq drops the most since pandemic as Democratic ‘blue wave’ upends AI bets
item.description: Investors fear newly elected politicians up and down the US will seek to slow data centre development in blow to tech stocks

item.title: [Euractiv] A (Chinese) burn
item.description: Tonight's edition also includes: Giorgia Meloni frustated over proliferation of diplomatic formats and initiatives

item.title: [Politico Europe] CBD edibles can’t be labeled organic, says EU court
item.description: Luxembourg’s judges tell the hemp lobby the label comes after the paperwork.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage says he’ll meet Le Pen ‘at some point in time’
item.description: The Reform leader's comments came after POLITICO reported that the French far-right leader was keeping Farage hanging on a desired Paris rendezvous.

item.title: [Politico Europe] La fin accélérée du macronisme au Parlement
item.description: Scène inédite à l’Assemblée mercredi soir : la première partie du budget de l’Etat a été rejetée à l’unanimité. Comment expliquer qu’aucun député n’ait approuvé le texte issu des débats. Pourquoi les députés du centre et de la droite sont agacés par Sébastien Lecornu ? Quels sont les scénarios qui se dessinent pour la suite […]

item.title: [Euractiv] Fincantieri, Navantia and Naval Group advance European corvette programme
item.description: The project reflects the need to overcome fragmentation in Europe's naval industry

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Drug trafficking is ramping in Europe, why and what are the consequences ?
item.description: The trial of 5 men suspected of brutal killings associated with France’s major drug cartel should come to an end in Aix-en Provence this Friday (6th of November).

item.title: [EU Observer] Chinese spy suspect walks free after Prague court acquittal, while Czech spy suspect in China remains behind bars
item.description: Yang Yiming, a suspected Chinese spy, has walked free after a Czech court acquitted him, but prosecutors have appealed the verdict. However, Czech national Aleš K. is still behind bars in China for allegedly breaching the country's security laws.

item.title: [EU Observer] Chief trade MEP Bernd Lange slams EU Commission for ‘hiding’ behind voting rules on banning Israeli settlement imports
item.description: MEPs scolded the EU Commission for failing to propose legislation on banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements.

item.title: [Financial Times] AI backlash threatens trillion-dollar data centre boom, say tech leaders
item.description: Executives at FT’s Future of AI summit admit tech industry has fuelled hostility towards its own expansion

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs at odds with the public as poll shows huge majority against loosening pesticide rules
item.description: Between 68-80 percent of Europeans across seven EU states want to phase-out rather than increase pesticide use, according to a new poll. But MEPs appear determined to go in the other direction.

item.title: [Euractiv] Biotech Act: MEPs push ahead on clinical trials, but SPC talks stall
item.description: Lawmakers propose creating a new Clinical Trials Expert Committee

item.title: [Euractiv] EU faces storm with ‘a small umbrella with holes’
item.description: Budget commissioner urges national capitals to overcome new 'own resource' deadlock to fund EU

item.title: [Euractiv] Kremlin denies Russia role in fridge cyberattacks
item.description: Grocery stores in at least nine European countries face hundreds of millions in food losses

item.title: [Politico Europe] France, US clash over G7 effort on AI safety
item.description: White House slams proposal by France for G7 oversight as “unnecessary bureaucracy.”

item.title: [EU Observer] Details emerge of Russian atrocity: dropping three-tonne bombs on civilians at food bank and shelter (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,715)
item.description: Newly released police body-camera footage and analysis by independent Russian investigators puncture Moscow’s claims they hit a “military target”, exposing how rescue workers and civilians were lured into a shelter in Komyshuvakha before being annihilated.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Meloni urges ‘disorganized’ EU to speak with one voice on Ukraine
item.description: The Italian prime minister slammed Europe's engagement with Ukraine peace talks as "all over the place."

item.title: [Politico Europe] Mélenchon’s mission for his young fans: Debate boomers on Facebook
item.description: The leftist presidential candidate is betting that his young supporters can win over their parents on the old-school social network.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU ‘closely monitoring’ aircraft bomb hoaxes
item.description: Brussels has activated EU-level aviation security information sharing mechanism

item.title: [Euractiv] Talks ‘well underway’ for partial German takeover of tank maker KNDS: source
item.description: The move would jettison previous plans to float a share of KNDS on financial markets via an initial public offering

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Emotional part’ of Polish court crisis is ‘closer to over’ says Tusk, amid talks of EU mediation
item.description: The "very emotional part" of a conflict between the government and right-wing Polish president Karol Nawrocki over the appointment of judges and ambassadors is almost over, according to prime minister Donald Tusk.

item.title: [Politico Europe] How NATO can turn data into defense advantage
item.description: In a world where conflict outcomes are increasingly defined by information advantage, military leaders must treat data as a primary combat asset.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Burnham won’t follow Trump in actively inviting Putin to G20
item.description: Britain has been one of Ukraine's staunchest allies since Russia's full-scale invasion of the country in 2022.

item.title: [Euractiv] Democrats’ midterm victory unlikely to sway Trump on Ukraine
item.description: Presidential veto powers and limited weapons stocks could hamper additional deliveries to Kyiv, analysts warn

item.title: [Euractiv] Meloni protests EU disarray as Brussels hosts Ukraine talks
item.description: Italian leader protests that the lack of a single EU voice at the table ‘is unacceptable’

item.title: [Euractiv] Dublin seeks to rein in Franco-German car emissions deal
item.description: Irish proposal would deny zero-emission status to cars running on clean fuels

item.title: [Euractiv] Parliament’s two biggest groups to co-lead EU Kids Act
item.description: EPP and S&D will share rapporteurship of Commission's online child safety law

item.title: [Euractiv] Beijing warns EU against deploying anti-China trade weapons
item.description: Brussels is preparing an armoury of new trade tools to potentially wield against Beijing

item.title: [Euractiv] Bulgaria’s spending on generic medicines drastically below EU average [Partner Content]
item.description: Generic medicines account for 75% of pharmaceutical sales by volume in Bulgaria with less than 10% of public funding

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe should beware of buying America’s increasingly unaccountable AI killing-machines
item.description: As Washington hands its autonomous warfare roadmap to Musk and other defence-industry moguls, European leaders in Geneva must decide whether to copy a model that speeds up killing, while hollowing out accountability for civilian deaths.

item.title: [EU Observer] No EU appetite for Russian gas so far, as US and European negotiators discuss Ukraine peace deal
item.description: "The EU is sticking to abandoning fossil-fuel dependency on Russia," said one diplomat, as US, EU, and Ukrainian negotiators meet in Brussels, following reports of US pressure to resume Russian gas imports as part of a peace deal.

item.title: [Financial Times] Morning in America, twilight in the markets
item.description: Astonishing midterm election results will not repeal the turn of business and financial cycles

item.title: [Financial Times] The next US presidential race has begun
item.description: The Republicans and Democrats positioning themselves for a run at the Oval Office in 2028

item.title: [Financial Times] US midterm results herald upheaval in Middle East policy
item.description: American voters — including vice-president JD Vance — want an end to Trump’s Iran war and Washington’s proximity to Israel

item.title: [Financial Times] Democratic wave keeps US wealth taxes alive despite California loss
item.description: Proposition 40 billionaire tax set to be defeated in a rare victory for mega-donors in the US midterms

item.title: [DW] Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
item.description: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

item.title: [DW] Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
item.description: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

item.title: [DW] Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
item.description: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

item.title: [DW] Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
item.description: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

item.title: [DW] How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
item.description: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

item.title: [DW] Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

item.title: [DW] What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
item.description: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?
